title: Al-Ahkam al-Sultaniyya
author: al-mawardi
attributionNote: The attribution is the one the manuscript tradition and the scholarship give.
description: Al-Mawardi's account of the institutions of the caliphate and the offices that govern under it: the imamate, the vizierate, provincial governors, judges, the market inspector, the treasury and the conduct of war. Each office is defined by its duties, qualifications and limits, in the language of law rather than of political advice.
historicalContext: Written in Baghdad under the Abbasid caliphs, when the Buyid amirs held real power and the caliph's authority was largely formal. The book is both a legal description of government and an argument for restoring the caliphate's place within a divided polity.
availabilityNote: Arabic text only, streamed from OpenITI at read time. No English translation is included because no public-domain English translation was verified. Only the catalogue record, chapter outline and passage index are held here.
